text:
4.0 moles of argon and 5.0 moles of PCl$_{5}$ are introduced into an evacuated flask of 100 litre capacity at 610 K. The system is allowed to equilibrate. At equilibrium, the total pressure of mixture was found to be 6.0 atm. The $K_{p}$ for the reaction is :

[Given : R = 0.082 L atm $K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Here 4 moles of inert gas argon also present.

$\therefore$ Total moles of mixture present at equilibrium,

$n_{T} = 5 + x + 4$

= 9 + x

At equilibrium, total pressure $(p_{T}) = 6$ atm

Volume (v) = 100 L

Temperature = 610 K

$\therefore$ Using ideal gas equation,

$P_{T}V=n_{T}RT$

$\Rightarrow 6\times 100=(9+x)\times 0.082\times 610$

$\Rightarrow x=3$

Now,

$K_{P}=\frac{P_{PCl3}\times P_{Cl2}}{P_{PCl5}}$

$=\frac{\left [\frac{3}{9+3}\times 6\right ]\times \left [\frac{3}{9+3}\times 6\right ]}{\left [\frac{5-3}{9+3}\times 6\right ]}$

$=\frac{27}{12}$

$=\frac{9}{4}$

= 2.25 atm

Note :

Inert gas always contribute to total mole and pressure calculation.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : The first ionization enthalpy for oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen.

Reason R : The four electrons in 2p orbitals of oxygen experience more electron-electron repulsion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In nitrogen ($2p^{3}$) the three $2p$ electrons occupy separate orbitals, while in oxygen ($2p^{4}$) two of the four $2p$ electrons must share one orbital.

The four $2p$ electrons of oxygen therefore experience greater electron–electron repulsion, so the fourth $2p$ electron is removed more easily than a $2p$ electron of nitrogen; the first ionisation enthalpy of O (about $1314\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is lower than that of N (about $1402\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$).

Both A and R are correct, and the greater repulsion stated in R is the reason for A.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements.

$\bullet$ Statement I : In CuSO$_{4} . 5H_{2}O, Cu-O$ bonds are present.

$\bullet$ Statement II : In CuSO$_{4} . 5H_{2}O$, ligands coordinating with Cu(II) ion are O-and S-based ligands.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}\cdot 5\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ four water molecules are coordinated to $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ through their oxygen atoms, giving $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$; the fifth water molecule is held by hydrogen bonds between a coordinated water molecule and the sulphate ion.


[IMG]

Cu–O coordinate bonds are therefore present, so Statement I is correct.

In the crystal the remaining two axial positions around Cu are taken by oxygen atoms of sulphate ions. The S atom of sulphate is bonded to four O atoms and carries no lone pair, so it never acts as a donor; every donor atom around $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is oxygen, and Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: Two isomers (A) and (B) with Molar mass 184 g/mol and elemental composition C, 52.2%; H, 4.9% and Br 42.9% gave benzoic acid and p-bromobenzoic acid, respectively on oxidation with KMnO$_{4}$. Isomer 'A' is optically active and gives a pale yellow precipitate when warmed with alcoholic AgNO$_{3}$. Isomer 'A' and 'B' are, respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In 184 g of the compound: C $=\dfrac{0.522\times 184}{12}=8$, H $=\dfrac{0.049\times 184}{1}=9$, Br $=\dfrac{0.429\times 184}{80}\approx 1$, so both isomers are $\mathrm{C}{}_{8}\mathrm{H}{}_{9}\mathrm{Br}$.

Hot $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ oxidises every side chain having a benzylic H to $-\mathrm{COOH}$, so each isomer has one two-carbon side chain on the ring.

A gives benzoic acid, so Br is on the side chain; A is optically active, so the side chain carries a stereocentre: A $=\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{Br})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. Being a secondary benzylic bromide, it ionises on warming with alcoholic $\mathrm{AgNO}{}_{3}$ and gives a pale yellow precipitate of AgBr.

B gives p-bromobenzoic acid, so Br is on the ring para to an ethyl group: B $=p\text{-}\mathrm{BrC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (achiral).


[IMG]

The o-methylbenzyl bromide in (A) and (B) is achiral and would give phthalic acid on oxidation.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text:
A box contains 0.90 g of liquid water in equilibrium with water vapour at 27${}^{\circ }$C. The equilibrium vapour pressure of water at 27${}^{\circ }$C is 32.0 Torr. When the volume of the box is increased, some of the liquid water evaporates to maintain the equilibrium pressure. If all the liquid water evaporates, then the volume of the box must be $__________$ litre. [nearest integer]

(Given : R = 0.082 L atm $K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1})$

(Ignore the volume of the liquid water and assume water vapours behave as an ideal gas.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, 760 Torr = 1 atm

$\therefore$ 32 Torr = $\frac{32}{760}$ atm

As all the liquid water evaporates so entire water is in gaseous state.

$\therefore$ Weight of water vapour = 0.9 g

$\therefore$ Moles of water vapour (n) = $\frac{0.9}{18}$

Pressure (P) = $\frac{32}{760}$ atm

Temperature (T) = (27 + 273) K = 300 K

R = 0.082 L atm $K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

Given water vapour act as an ideal gas, so we can apply ideal gas equation.

From ideal gas equation,

PV = nRT

$\Rightarrow \frac{32}{760}\times v=\frac{0.9}{18}\times 0.082\times 300$

$\Rightarrow v=29$ L
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text:
In the given reaction,

 
[IMG]


the number of $sp^{2}$ hybridised carbon(s) in compound 'X' is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cyclohexanol is a secondary alcohol, so acidified $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}$ oxidises it to cyclohexanone.

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}$ adds to the carbonyl group, and hydrolysis gives the tertiary alcohol 1-phenylcyclohexan-1-ol.

With $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ and heat this tertiary alcohol dehydrates to the conjugated alkene 1-phenylcyclohexene, which is X.


[IMG]

In X, the six carbons of the benzene ring and the two carbons of the ring $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ double bond are $sp^{2}$ hybridised; the other four ($\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$) carbons of the cyclohexene ring are $sp^{3}$.

Number of $sp^{2}$ carbons $=6+2=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift
